question: Do frozen numerical ear-EEG descriptors recur across two nights of the same source participant, and how does the existing transition detector transfer to a new in-ear acquisition?
freeze_stage: Metadata-only selection, before downloading or analyzing these raw signals. No outcome-based cohort or parameter selection.
reserve: All other participants and all other sessions remain waveform-unexposed by this project; other sessions of exposed participants are not new-person holdouts.
analysis_selection: First four native recording hours, without interpreting calibration, diaries, triggers or sleep stages. Full raw files are retained and technically qualified; unused later hours remain unanalyzed. If shorter than four hours, quarantine for this experiment without replacement.
input_contract: Numeric discovery receives only ear-channel microvolt arrays, sample rate and technical validity. Subject/session identifiers are restricted to curator and paired evaluator. No PSG, questionnaire, stage, diagnosis, demographic, text or inferred meaning is used.
reference: Native average reference, preserved. In-ear is a new montage; it is not equivalent to cEEGrid or Neurable.
primary_descriptor: For each view, coordinatewise median of QC-pass feature rows, standardized by frozen Experiment003 training median/IQR. Session distance is root-mean-square difference across view coordinates. This summarizes distributions; it does not align individual events between nights.
primary_statistic: For each view, mean same-participant session1/session2 distance compared with mean different-participant cross-session distance. Exact permutation distribution of the matched mean over all assignments of session2 summaries; lower-tail fraction including observed assignment. Minimum three complete pairs. Report raw p and three-view Bonferroni p, without a universal or biological specificity claim.
secondary: Per-record QC-pass fraction and invalid windows
Per-view primary-scale event count and rate per scored-center minute
Within-record pairwise boundary agreement with exact event denominators
Full cross-session distance matrix and all pairing permutation statistics
uncertainty: Six participants maximum; repeated windows are not independent samples. Record all exclusions and paired denominators; no window-level confidence intervals. This selected six-person sample is not population-representative. Exact pairing permutation assumes exchangeable cross-person assignments; stable anatomy, montage, artifact and reference effects can drive apparent recurrence.
claims: No pretrained LLM inference, mental-state decoding, clinical diagnosis, universal geometry, or physical Neurable validation. Greater same-person similarity may indicate person/device-specific structure rather than universal tokens.
failure_policy: Preserve candidates and raw hashes; quarantine source/channel/rate/unit/duration inconsistencies. Missing/nonfinite samples remain invalid. Preserve native gaps and do not join context across them. No pair replacement, imputation, parameter tuning or threshold refitting. Publish null or weak results. Corrections require a recorded new run.
